issues.description: Field and constructor parameter types for StockIngredient.price are inconsistent: The problem statement UML (StockIngredient) declares price as int (UML lists -price: int and constructor StockIngredient(String, int, int)). The solution implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/StockIngredient.java) uses int for the price field and constructor parameter. The template implementation (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/StockIngredient.java) declares price as double and the constructor parameter as double. This mismatch can confuse students about which numeric type to use for prices and may lead to subtle type-related issues when implementing calculateTotalPrice or acceptSupplyDelivery (e.g., unexpected casting, rounding, or failing to match the expected signatures in tests).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the type of StockIngredient.price consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fix to match the UML and solution: change the template file src/de/tum/cit/ase/StockIngredient.java to use int for the price field and constructor parameter and have getPrice() return int (update field declaration, constructor signature parameter type, and getPrice return type). Alternatively, if fractional prices are required, update the problem statement UML and the solution implementation to use double uniformly (and update method documentation and any code that sums or compares prices).
